name: The Andorhal cult cell (the eight sentries, the runner, the masked crew)

physicalDetails.detail: Fenner's yard (eight, per Cyndia's count): two at the near corner of the rope-walk, weight square on both feet, hands empty, a clear foot off the wall; a pair at the trough drinking one at a time, one always facing the lane, changing over silently; one on the hoist platform, who stops coiling rope and surveys the whole yard; three sitting by the gate, the middle one with his cap on, the other two keeping their feet under them. Placed so that between them they hold the yard, both ends of the shed and the mouth of the lane. The pair at the trough turn their heads away from the lamp when it is lit.

The runner (one of the eight; the hoist man): big, going soft, brown beard, a loader's leather pad on one shoulder, no mask. Walks up Hurdle Lane with his eyes front, passes Sylvanas and Havel close without looking (every other man in the yard looked at Havel at least once); presses something into a crack in the wall at hip height without checking behind him; goes to Kett's by Tenter Row.

Kett's loft (five masked): waxed cloth over nose and mouth with a dull shine, the same kind as the cloth over the jar's mouth under Brask's floor; long leather gloves to the forearm. One with a crock between his feet, scooping something dark and thick that hangs off his fingers 'like cold dripping' and working it into open sacks with his forearm buried in the grain; a second rolls the mouth and sews the sack shut with a long needle; a third carries closed sacks to a stack by the stair. At the window a man peels off gloves one at a time without touching skin, drops them in a bucket, washes hands and forearms in a basin, only then lowers the cloth to drink from a jug with his head turned away from the sacks.

voiceMarkers.detail: None heard. The runner and the masked man talk briefly at the top of the stair; Sylvanas cannot hear it. The man with the crock keeps his gloved hands held up and away from both their bodies.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Keep sewing the night's sacks onto wagons for the first carts out; keep the loaders locked into the rope-walk and sentries posted; three of the gate-sitters go up Hurdle Lane toward Tenter Row.
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Unknown. Handlers and workers are separated by layer.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Calm, drilled, secure. The cult 'thinks the city's theirs' (Sylvanas). One masked man looks at the window for a long time and then returns to work: either he saw nothing or he has been taught to stand like that.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: The window man looks toward Sylvanas's roof after a grit slide, stands with bare hands out from his sides, does not go to the stair and does not call anyone, then picks up his needle. Not known whether Sylvanas was seen.

At the bell the crew at Fenner's answer with doors and wheels: the rope-walk crew go into the door at the far end and lock it from inside (Cyndia, watching from Havel's side); the pair from the trough go in last together; the three from the gate go up Hurdle Lane toward Tenter Row.

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Discipline: sentries placed as a trained watch would be (corner, trough, platform, gate), pairs that move and stop together, trade places without speech, and keep their eyes off the militia captain.

Two layers of staff: an outer layer of watchers/couriers (the eight, the runner) and an inner layer of masked contaminators at Kett's; the courier stays out of the loft proper and talks at the stair head.
Dead drops in wall cracks at hip height (the runner), a courier chain between Fenner's yard and Kett's loft.
Skilled alchemical and necromantic hands (Jaina's inference): a coat applied to the grain by hand between dressing and sewing.

Self-protection: wax cloths, long gloves, gloves removed without touching skin and dropped in a bucket, forearms washed before drinking; the masked men protect themselves from the grain, not from dust.

howOthersAddressThem.speaker: Havel
howOthersAddressThem.pattern: 'the loaders', 'that lot', 'the crew', 'them'. No names given for any.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Trained waiting: weight even on both feet, hands empty, clear of walls; faces to the lane; changeovers without a word. Sylvanas links it in thought to Tam on the hoist at Brask's granary (the boy who bit open his own collar sooner than speak to her).

knowledge.detail: Not shown. They know the grain is dangerous to handle and protect themselves from it. They hold the north-bound custom of the loaders in locked sheds and have been on the lane since midsummer (the first lot) and Lammas (the gate three).

arc.currentPosition: At the end of Chapter 7 the party plans to take one living man from Kett's loft that night. Count so far: eight at Fenner's (including the runner), five masked at Kett's, and 'more of them' (the three from the gate) heading up Hurdle Lane. At least thirteen are seen on the page.
